scenario: A press release announcing a new regional office, already published on the company website.
why: It has been approved and released for anyone to read, so sharing it causes no harm.

scenario: The internal phone directory listing colleague names and desk extensions.
why: It is meant for colleagues only. Outsiders could use it to target staff, but disclosure causes limited harm.

scenario: A signed client contract showing negotiated pricing, service levels and renewal dates.
why: Contracts carry confidentiality obligations. A leak could breach them and damage the client relationship.

scenario: A completed background-screening report for a job applicant.
why: The report contains highly sensitive personal and potentially legal data about an identifiable individual.

scenario: A file containing emergency access retrieval steps and admin credentials.
why: Authentication credentials could directly enable unauthorized privileged access and require the highest protection.
